title: Grateful Dead Live at Omaha Civic Auditorium on 1973-10-21

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of a Fall ’73 show with Keith’s piano shining and standout El Paso, though occasional tape hiss and splice mar the otherwise solid performance.
ai_review.review: The set captures a classic autumn‑1973 Dead run – Keith Godchaux’s piano is highlighted on Here Comes Sunshine and throughout the night, while the band delivers memorable moments in El Paso, Cumberland Blues and the half‑step/Big River/PITB sequence. Recording-wise the tape has hiss, static patches and a splice on Wharf Rat, but the mix remains generally clear enough to enjoy the strong playing of Jerry’s leads and Bill’s jazzy drums.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (especially Keith, Jerry and Bill) with several 5‑star comments; technical flaws are noted but not enough to outweigh the show’s strengths, yielding an overall solid rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape hiss and static in parts of the first set, a splice on Wharf Rat, occasional unclear sections (e.g., Here Comes Sunshine jam), but overall a decent mix with instruments fairly balanced.

standout_songs: Playing In The Band > Half Step > Big River > Playing In The Band
poor_songs: Beat It On Down The Line (blown start)
Here Comes Sunshine (jam muffled in first set)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set starts unevenly with some sound issues but gains momentum by the middle; the second set builds energy with a powerful half‑step/Big River/PITB sequence and peaks during He's Gone into Truckin', delivering an overall satisfying arc despite occasional lapses.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for sweet, melodic leads, high notes on He's Gone, and generally pleasant vocals throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for laying down solid bass foundations early, later producing a huge, almost feedback‑laden tone that some felt got lost in the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned as strumming away and contributing vocals, though a few reviewers felt his presence was less noticeable during extended jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux receives abundant praise for exceptional piano work, with moments described as “wonderful,” “pounding amazing chords,” and even “electric sneezes” that add character.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (Mickey) is highlighted for jazzy, high‑energy drumming; his mix is often turned up, creating a driving rhythm especially on Black Throated Wind.
